questions.question:
Identify the part of the sentence that contains a grammatical error.

A. The main affect B. of the new policy C. will be an increase D. in productivity.

options.text: The main affect
of the new policy
will be an increase
in productivity

questions.solution:
The correct answer is '1' i.e. The main affect .

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The error in the sentence lies in the word **'affect'**. It is incorrectly used as a noun.
 
• The correct word should be **'effect'**, which is the appropriate noun form.
 
• In English, **'affect'** is primarily used as a verb meaning "to influence," while **'effect'** is a noun meaning "a result or outcome."

Correct sentence: *The main effect of the new policy will be an increase in productivity*.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **'Affect' vs 'Effect':**
 
 
• **Affect (verb):** To influence something. Example: The weather affects my mood.
 
• **Effect (noun):** A result or outcome. Example: The medication had a positive effect on her health.
 
 
 
• **Usage Tip:** If you're looking for a noun, use "effect." If you're describing an action, use "affect."
</ul

questions.question:
Which of the following sentences uses the word "minute" with the **same meaning** as in the following sentence?

"The microscope revealed a minute speck of dust"

options.text: The meeting will start in a few minutes.
I was just a minute away from being late.
The camera captured every minute detail of the insect’s wing.
The alarm went off in exactly sixty seconds, or one minute.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is '3' i.e. The camera captured every minute detail of the insect’s wing .

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word **"minute"** in the given sentence refers to something **extremely small** or **tiny**.
 
• Option 3 uses the word "minute" with the same meaning, emphasizing the **tiny details** captured by the camera.
 
• Other options, such as 1, 2, and 4, refer to "minute" as a unit of time, which is not the intended meaning in the given sentence.

Correct sentence: *The camera captured every minute detail of the insect’s wing.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The word "minute" has two distinct meanings:
 
 
• **Time-related:** Refers to a unit of time equivalent to 60 seconds (e.g., "The meeting will start in a few minutes").
 
• **Size-related:** Refers to something extremely small or detailed (e.g., "A minute speck of dust").
 
 
 
• Understanding the context of the sentence is crucial to determining the correct meaning of the word.
</ul

questions.question: According to the passage, what has been one of the positive impacts of technological advances?

options.text: Automation has reduced job loss
Medical advances such as gene editing and precision medicine promise to cure previously incurable diseases
Communication technology has caused more isolation
Technological advances have had no impact on the standard of living

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The passage highlights several positive impacts of progress, specifically noting that "**Medical advances like gene editing and precision medicine hold the promise to cure diseases that were once thought incurable.**"
 
• It also mentions that technological advances have generally provided "**standards of living much better**" and improved global cooperation through communication technology.
 
• Option 2 directly mirrors the text's description of medical progress as a revolutionary change.
 
• Other options represent negative impacts or factually incorrect statements based on the text (e.g., automation is causing job loss, not reducing it).

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

**Correct Sentence from Text:** *"Medical advances like **gene editing and precision medicine** hold the promise to **cure diseases that were once thought incurable**."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1:** Incorrect. The passage states that "**Automation is taking away jobs** for millions of people," which is a negative impact.
 
• **Option 3:** Incorrect. The text states communication technology has allowed people to "**work together across borders**," rather than causing isolation.
 
• **Option 4:** Incorrect. The author explicitly states that technological advances "**have provided standards of living much better**."

questions.question: What negative consequence of technology is mentioned in the passage?

options.text: It makes life more comfortable
It creates a sense of disconnection and fear for the future
It helps people across borders and cultures
It eliminates the need for privacy

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The passage notes that the "**speed of innovation has left millions behind**," which results in a "**feeling of disconnection, fear for the future**."
 
• This is presented as a negative consequence alongside **automation taking away jobs** and the erosion of "what it means to be human."
 
• The author also points out that our **dependence on technology** is raising critical concerns regarding "privacy, security, and freedom."
 
• Option 2 directly reflects the text's description of the psychological and social impact of rapid technological change.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

**Correct Sentence from Text:** *"The speed of innovation has left millions behind, and with it there is a **feeling of disconnection, fear for the future**."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1:** Incorrect. Making life more comfortable (better standards of living) is described by the author as a **positive** impact.
 
• **Option 3:** Incorrect. Helping people work together across borders is listed as a **positive** result of communication technology.
 
• **Option 4:** Incorrect. The passage states that technology creates "**questions regarding privacy**," not that it eliminates the *need* for it; rather, it makes privacy more vulnerable.

questions.question: What question does the passage raise about our relationship with technology?

options.text: How can we make technology more affordable?
How can we use technology to solve political conflicts?
Are we masters of technology, or is technology the master of us?
Should we stop using technology altogether?

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The passage explores the shifting dynamic between humans and their inventions, particularly as **AI and automation** become deeply integrated into daily life.
 
• The author explicitly poses a philosophical question regarding our agency: "**are we Master of Technology, or is technology the master of us?**"
 
• This question arises from the **paradox of progress**, where our growing dependence on technology creates concerns about privacy, security, and the erosion of human identity.
 
• The text suggests that while we use technology to solve problems, the power it holds over social structures makes our **control over it** a central theme.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

**Correct Sentence from Text:** *"As we introduce Al into everyday life, do we have to sit back and ask ourselves: **are we Master of Technology, or is technology the master of us?**"*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1:** Incorrect. The text focuses on the **social and ethical implications** of technology rather than its economic affordability.
 
• **Option 2:** Incorrect. While the text mentions working across "borders and cultures," it does not specifically discuss **political conflicts**.
 
• **Option 4:** Incorrect. The author does not suggest a complete **rejection of technology**; instead, they advocate for resolving new issues to ensure a "more just and sustainable tomorrow."

questions.question: What does the passage suggest is necessary to make progress more just and sustainable?

options.text: Increasing dependence on technology
Resolving the new issues brought by technology
Limiting technological innovations
Relying solely on automation to solve problems

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The passage identifies a **"double-edged nature"** of progress, where technology provides solutions to big problems but simultaneously introduces new, complex challenges.
 
• The author explicitly states that for progress to lead to a **"more just and sustainable tomorrow,"** human beings must take the initiative to **"resolve"** these new issues.
 
• These issues include **job displacement** via automation, **privacy and security** concerns, and the **social disconnection** caused by the rapid pace of innovation.
 
• Option 2 directly captures the author's concluding argument that human intervention and problem-solving are required to navigate the paradox of technology.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

**Correct Sentence from Text:** *"On one hand, technology comes bearing answers to some of humankind's biggest problems, yet it also brings **new issues that human beings must resolve in order to make progress mean a more just and sustainable tomorrow.**"*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1:** Incorrect. The text lists **"dependence on technology"** as a cause of ethical questions regarding freedom and security, not as a requirement for sustainability.
 
• **Option 3:** Incorrect. The passage describes technological breakthroughs as part of **"human evolution"**; the focus is on resolving the side effects of innovation rather than halting innovation itself.
 
• **Option 4:** Incorrect. The text presents **automation** as a potential threat to millions of jobs, making it an issue to be managed rather than the primary solution for a just future.

questions.question: Choose the correct meaning of the idiom: **Part and parcel**

options.text: A small, unimportant detail
A non-essential part of a whole
An integral and unavoidable component
A delivery service for packages

questions.solution:
The correct answer is '3' i.e. An integral and unavoidable component .

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The idiom **"Part and parcel"** means an essential or integral part of something.
 
• It refers to something that is unavoidable or inherent in a particular situation or process.
 
• For example, "Stress is part and parcel of being a doctor," means stress is an unavoidable component of the profession.

Correct sentence: *Hard work is part and parcel of success in life.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Idioms are phrases or expressions that have a figurative meaning different from their literal meaning.
 
• Understanding idioms is essential for improving language fluency and comprehension, as they are commonly used in both spoken and written communication.
</ul

questions.question: Select the most appropriate antonym of the word: **Credulous**

options.text: Trusting
Skeptical
Gullible
Naive

questions.solution:
The correct answer is '2' i.e. Skeptical .

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word **Credulous** refers to someone who is too willing to believe things without questioning them, often described as gullible or naive.
 
• Among the given options:
 
 
• **Trusting:** Similar to credulous, as it implies belief without doubt.
 
• **Skeptical:** The opposite of credulous, as it refers to someone who is doubtful and questions things.
 
• **Gullible:** Synonymous with credulous, indicating someone easily deceived.
 
• **Naive:** Related to credulous, as it implies a lack of experience or sophistication.
 
 
 
• Thus, the most appropriate antonym is **Skeptical**.

Correct sentence: *The most appropriate antonym of "Credulous" is **Skeptical**.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Antonyms are words with opposite meanings. In this case:
 
 
• **Credulous:** Tends to believe things easily.
 
• **Skeptical:** Doubts or questions the truth of things.
 
 
 
• It is important to distinguish between synonyms (similar meanings) and antonyms (opposite meanings).
</ul

questions.question:
Choose the correct one-word substitute for:
A large-scale departure of people from one place

options.text: Exodus
Emigration
Immigration
Migration

questions.solution:
The correct answer is '1' i.e. Exodus .

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• An **Exodus** refers to a large-scale departure or movement of people from one place to another, usually due to certain circumstances like war, famine, or other crises.
 
• The word **Emigration** (Option 2) refers to leaving one’s own country to settle in another, which is not necessarily on a large scale.
 
• The word **Immigration** (Option 3) refers to coming to live in a country permanently, which is the opposite of emigration.
 
• **Migration** (Option 4) refers to the movement of people or animals from one place to another, but it may not necessarily mean a large-scale departure.

Correct sentence: *A large-scale departure of people from one place is called an **Exodus**.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Exodus in History:**
 
 
• The term is often associated with the biblical account of the Israelites leaving Egypt under the leadership of Moses, which is considered a significant historical exodus.
 
 
 
• **Modern Examples:**
 
 
• Mass departures due to wars, natural disasters, or political instability are often described as exoduses.

questions.question:
**Change the following sentence into the Active form.**

A new bridge is being constructed by the city council.

options.text: The city council is constructing a new bridge.
A new bridge constructed the city council.
The city council constructed a new bridge.
The city council has constructed a new bridge.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is '1' i.e. The city council is constructing a new bridge .

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence is in the **passive voice**. The structure is "**A new bridge is being constructed by the city council**."
 
• To convert a sentence from **passive** to **active** voice, the subject (doer of the action) becomes the focus of the sentence.
 
• In the active voice, the **subject** "the city council" is performing the action of constructing the bridge.
 
• The correct sentence in the active voice is: **"The city council is constructing a new bridge."**

Correct sentence: *The city council is constructing a new bridge*.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Active vs. Passive Voice:**

 
 
• **Active Voice:** The subject performs the action. Example: "The cat chased the mouse."
 
• **Passive Voice:** The subject is acted upon. Example: "The mouse was chased by the cat."
 
 
 
• **When to Use Active Voice:**
 
 
• Use active voice for clear and direct sentences.
 
• Example: "She is writing a book" (active) vs. "A book is being written by her" (passive).
 
 
</ul

questions.question: Select the most appropriate antonym of the word: **Ineffable**

options.text: Expressible
Inarticulate
Unfathomable
Indescribable

questions.solution:
The correct answer is '1' i.e. Expressible.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word "**Ineffable**" means something that is too great or extreme to be expressed or described in words.
 
• To find an antonym, we must look for a word that means the opposite – i.e., something that *can* be expressed or described.
 
• Among the given options:
 
 
• **1) Expressible:** Means something that can be expressed, making it the correct antonym of "ineffable."
 
• **2) Inarticulate:** Means unable to express oneself clearly, which is not the opposite of ineffable.
 
• **3) Unfathomable:** Means difficult or impossible to understand, which is a synonym of ineffable, not an antonym.
 
• **4) Indescribable:** Means something that cannot be described, which is again a synonym of ineffable.
 
 

Correct answer: *The most appropriate antonym of "Ineffable" is "Expressible."*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Synonyms of "Ineffable":** Indescribable, unutterable, inexpressible.
 
• **Antonyms of "Ineffable":** Expressible, describable, definable.

questions.question:

The manager said, "We will make a decision by Friday."

options.text: The manager said that they would make a decision by Friday.
The manager said that we would make a decision by Friday.
The manager said that they will make a decision by Friday.
The manager said that we will make a decision by Friday.

questions.solution:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence is in **direct speech**, and the task is to convert it into **indirect speech**.
 
• In indirect speech, changes are made to the pronouns and tense, and the quotation marks are removed.
 
• Here, the direct speech is in the **future tense** ("We will make"), which changes to the **future in the past** tense ("they would make").
 
• Additionally, the pronoun "we" changes to "they" to match the indirect speech.

Correct sentence: *The manager said that they **would make** a decision by Friday.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Changes in tense when converting to indirect speech:**
 
 
• Simple present → Simple past
 
• Present continuous → Past continuous
 
• Future simple ("will") → Future in the past ("would")
 
 
 
• **Pronoun changes:**
 
 
• "We" → "They" (depending on the subject).

options.text: it has originally have been designed for short one
it has originally been designed for short ones
it has originally was designed for short ones

questions.solution:

__

• The use of **“has been”** in the correct option highlights the past action of designing the Rover while maintaining relevance to the present context.
 
• The word **“ones”** is used to correctly replace the plural noun "short drives."

__

questions.question:
**Select the option that expresses the given sentence in direct voice.**

The manager told the team that their hard work and dedication had been noticed and appreciated.

options.text: The manager said, "Your hard work and dedication had been noticed and appreciated."
The manager said, "Your hard work and dedication have been noticed and appreciated."
The manager told the team, "Their hard work and dedication had been noticed and appreciated."
The manager said, "Their hard work and dedication were noticed and appreciated."

questions.solution:
The correct answer is '2' i.e. The manager said, "Your hard work and dedication have been noticed and appreciated."

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• To express the sentence in direct voice, we need to focus on the exact words spoken by the speaker.
 
• The direct speech should retain the original meaning and tense as conveyed in the indirect speech.
 
• The indirect sentence states that the manager told the team their hard work and dedication "had been noticed and appreciated," which implies past perfect tense. However, in direct speech, the context changes slightly to present perfect tense, as it reflects the immediate recognition.

Correct sentence: *The manager said, "Your hard work and dedication have been noticed and appreciated."*.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Understanding Direct Speech:**
 
 
• Direct speech involves quoting the exact words spoken by a person, enclosed in quotation marks.
 
• Example: He said, "I am going to the park."
 
 
 
• **Understanding Indirect Speech:**
 
 
• Indirect speech paraphrases what was said, often adjusting tense and pronouns.
 
• Example: He said that he was going to the park.

questions.question:
**Select the option that expresses the given sentence in direct voice.**

He asked me if I would have been able to finish the report that day if he had not helped me with the research, which had been a very tedious process.

options.text: "Would you have been able to finish the report today if I had not helped you with the research, which was a very tedious process?" he asked me.
"Will you have been able to finish the report today if I did not help you with the research, which was a very tedious process?" he asked me.
"Would you have been able to finish the report that day if I had not helped you with the research, which had been a very tedious process?" he asked me.
"Could you finish the report today if I had not helped you with the research, which was a very tedious process?" he asked me.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is '1' i.e. "Would you have been able to finish the report today if I had not helped you with the research, which was a very tedious process?" he asked me. .

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence is in **indirect speech**, where the speaker asks about a hypothetical situation in the past.
 
• To convert this into direct speech, we need to maintain the tense and structure of the original question.
 
• The structure in direct speech reflects the use of **would** in hypothetical situations, as it matches the reported question.

Correct sentence: *"Would you have been able to finish the report today if I had not helped you with the research, which was a very tedious process?" he asked me.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Direct Speech:** Involves quoting the exact words of the speaker, often enclosed in quotation marks.
 
• **Indirect Speech:** Involves paraphrasing the speaker's words without quotation marks, often changing the tense accordingly.
 
• **Key Rule:** In hypothetical questions, "would" is used to express unreal conditions.
</ul

questions.question:
**Rearrange the following sentence parts to form a meaningful and grammatically correct paragraph:**

P. She created a decadent batter and baked three layers of cake flawlessly.

Q. The finished cake was a stunning design, prepared for the celebration and the candles.

R. She coated the outside of the entire cake after stacking the layers with icing between them.

S. Before gently levelling each cake layer, she created a light and creamy icing.

options.text: S, P, R, Q
P, S, R, Q
Q, S, R, P
R, S, P, Q

questions.solution:
The correct answer is '2' i.e. P, S, R, Q .

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The paragraph should be logically arranged so that the sequence of events flows meaningfully and grammatically.
 
• Step 1: Sentence P introduces the preparation of the batter and baking of the cake layers.
 
• Step 2: Sentence S describes the preparation of the icing and the leveling of the cake layers.
 
• Step 3: Sentence R explains the stacking of the layers with icing and coating the cake.
 
• Step 4: Sentence Q concludes the paragraph by describing the finished product—ready for celebration.
 
• Thus, the correct sequence is P, S, R, Q.

Correct sentence sequence: *P. She created a decadent batter and baked three layers of cake flawlessly. S. Before gently leveling each cake layer, she created a light and creamy icing. R. She coated the outside of the entire cake after stacking the layers with icing between them. Q. The finished cake was a stunning design, prepared for the celebration and the candles.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Tips for paragraph arrangement:**
 
 
• Identify the introduction, main body, and conclusion of the paragraph.
 
• Look for logical connectors or keywords that indicate sequence, such as "first," "then," "after," etc.
 
• Ensure the paragraph maintains a coherent flow of ideas.
 
 
 
• In this case, the sequence of events aligns perfectly with option 2: P, S, R, Q.
